## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The ventilator package: a mechanical-ventilator simulator, ported from an existing stand-alone ventilator simulator
(`ventilator-sim-hamilton.html`), with a lung-pathology catalogue and the two-way link that couples it to the patient
engine. Each 20 ms tick the ventilator sends what it delivers (pressure, flow, volume, phase) and the engine sends the
patient's lung back (compliance, resistances, pleural pressure, effort). A clinician-educator gets the airway pressure
and flow picture of each lung pathology; an embedding developer gets the in-process and window links.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Equation of motion, single compartment: Paw + Pmus = V/C + R·Q + PEEP, with a non-linear recoil (airway closure,
  upper inflection, stress index), expiratory flow limitation and the patient's Pmus waveform, ported line for line from
  the original simulator (`mechanics.ts`).
- One ventilator step is 5 ms (4 Euler sub-steps of 1.25 ms), so one 20 ms engine tick is 4 steps (`vent.ts`).
- Expiratory resistance above the inspiratory one is expressed through the flow-limitation factor eflK = R_insp/R_exp
  without PEEP stenting, so R_exp is exactly the value given (`lung-input.ts`, `pathology/mechanics.ts`).
- Raised pleural pressure: when the end-expiratory pleural pressure exceeds PEEP by E = pleural − 5.44 − PEEP cmH2O
  (resting pleural −4 mmHg, Smith 2004), each breath must first raise alveolar pressure by E over 150 mL before tidal
  volume enters — the tension-pneumothorax picture (`pathology/mechanics.ts`).
- Catalogue rows at the reference settings (VC 490 mL, 14/min, PEEP 5, 60 L/min, 0.3 s pause): plateau = PEEP +
  auto-PEEP + VT/C, driving pressure = VT/C, peak − plateau = R_insp × 1 L/s; tests require each row's signature inside
  the clinically reported range (Miller 10e, Co-Existing Disease 8e, Dellinger 5e; `pathology/catalogue.ts`;
  `docs/physiology/vent-lung-pathology-data.md`).
- The frame sent to the engine carries the volume delivered since the breath started, so trapped gas (auto-PEEP) never
  inflates the engine's tidal volume; pause and inspiratory hold count as inspiration (`frame.ts`).
- The engine's `lungState` event is read as absolute values; shunt, dead space and FRC stay on the engine side
  (`lung-input.ts`).
- The engine is the master clock: the in-process link runs both in lockstep on one sim clock, and the window link runs
  the ventilator in real time × scale but never past the tick the monitor allows (`link/in-process.ts`,
  `link/vent-driver.ts`). To match the monitor's own ventilator, the volume-control flow is VT/Ti with
  Ti = 60/rate/(1 + I:E) and no pause (`link/core.ts`).
- Alarms keep the original simulator's banner rules and priority order, plus disconnection (a delivered breath that
  raised no pressure) and apnoea (`alarms.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

| `LINKED_MAX_FRAME_S` | `0.5` | s | — | FX-1: the longest animation frame a LINKED ventilator counts in full (wall s). Free-running it keeps v1.9's 0.1 s; linked, the engine's `clock` already bounds it (never more than MAX_AHEAD_TICKS ahead), and 0.1 s made a cockpit drawn at ≈ 5 frames/s (CI's Linux WebKit: 200–280 ms apart) run at half the session's speed — at ×4 it breathed for the patient at ×2, every frame late. Frames ≤ 0.1 s apart (any normal screen) step exactly as before. |
